authorship: Independently authored for SSC Prep Engine; no reference-paper stems, diagrams or options copied.

items.question: A seller sets a list price 40% above cost. A customer receives successive discounts of 10% and 20%. The marketplace keeps 5% of the amount the customer pays. Relative to cost, what is the seller's final profit or loss?
steps: Choose cost = 100; list price is 140.
After both discounts the customer pays 140 x 0.90 x 0.80 = 100.8.
The seller receives 100.8 x 0.95 = 95.76.
Loss is 100 - 95.76 = 4.24 per 100 of cost, or 4.24%.

wrong_options.3: Adds the discounts as 30% instead of multiplying their remaining-price factors.
wrong_options.4: Subtracts a fee of 5 per 100 of cost; the fee base is the customer's payment.

items.beginner_bridge: First practise one percentage change with an explicitly named base. Then combine two changes before introducing a fee.
items.shortcut_limit: Multiplying retention factors works because each rate applies to the amount after the preceding change. A fixed rupee fee needs subtraction instead.
items.mastery_check: Explain why the 5% fee cannot simply be subtracted from the gross profit percentage. Use a fresh independently authored example, not a replay of this answer.

items.question: A tank is initially one-sixth full. Pump A fills an empty tank in 30 minutes and pump B in 45 minutes. A drain empties a full tank in 90 minutes. All three are opened together. Pump B is then closed, while A and the drain stay open. If the tank first becomes full 24 minutes after the start, for how many minutes was B open?
steps: A minus the drain supplies 1/30 - 1/90 = 1/45 tank per minute throughout the 24 minutes.
Their contribution is 24/45 = 8/15 tank; initially there was 1/6 tank.
B must supply 1 - 1/6 - 8/15 = 3/10 tank.
At 1/45 tank per minute, B runs for (3/10) x 45 = 13.5 minutes. This is within the 24-minute window and both stage rates are positive.

wrong_options.1: Does not supply the required missing volume when substituted into the rate equation.
wrong_options.3: Solves a different missing-volume fraction; check the initial one-sixth.
wrong_options.4: Results in an overfilled tank at 24 minutes; it fails the volume check.

items.beginner_bridge: Convert each full-tank time into a per-minute rate. Introduce the drain separately, then model the switched pump.
items.shortcut_limit: The always-running net-rate method is valid only while those pumps and drains operate at constant rates.
items.mastery_check: Write and explain the equation 1/6 + 24/45 + t/45 = 1 before solving a new switch-time problem.

items.question: A cyclist completes a 72 km route in three equal-distance legs at 18, 24 and 36 km/h. There is one 10-minute stop between legs. What is the average speed for the entire outing, including the stop, rounded to two decimal places?
steps: Each leg is 24 km.
The stop adds 10/60 = 1/6 hour; total elapsed time is 19/6 hours.
Average speed is 72/(19/6) = 432/19 = 22.7368..., which rounds to 22.74 km/h.

wrong_options.2: Uses the arithmetic mean of the three speeds, which would require equal travel times.
wrong_options.4: Does not follow from total distance divided by total elapsed time; recheck minute-to-hour conversion.

items.beginner_bridge: Compare equal-time and equal-distance two-leg journeys before combining three legs and a stop.
items.shortcut_limit: The harmonic mean handles equal-distance moving legs, but an extra stop must still be added to total time.
items.mastery_check: Explain why the overall average must be below 24 km/h when the stop is included.

items.question: Three positive numbers have sum 9 and pairwise-product sum 23. Find the sum of their cubes minus three times their product.
steps: Write s = x+y+z = 9 and p = xy+yz+zx = 23.
The identity x^3+y^3+z^3-3xyz = s(s^2-3p) avoids solving separately for each number.
Substitute to obtain 9(81-69) = 108.
The data are feasible: 1, 3 and 5 have sum 9 and pairwise-product sum 3+15+5 = 23.

wrong_options.3: Multiplies s by p without the identity.
wrong_options.4: Uses the cube of the sum and ignores the cross terms.

items.beginner_bridge: Expand (x+y+z)^2 and group cross terms; then derive the cubic factorization with small integers.
items.shortcut_limit: An algebraic substitution is not enough if the givens contradict real-number constraints. Check that s^2 is at least 3p.
items.mastery_check: Explain why x^2+y^2+z^2 cannot be less than (x+y+z)^2/3 for real x, y, z.

items.question: Two circles have radii 5 cm and 12 cm, and their centres are 25 cm apart. Let L be the length between the points of contact on a direct common tangent, and M the corresponding length on a transverse common tangent. Find L^2 - M^2.
steps: A radius is perpendicular to its tangent. For the direct tangent the perpendicular offset is 12-5 = 7 cm.
For the transverse tangent the radii add, giving M^2 = 25^2 - 17^2 = 336.
The difference is 576-336 = 240 square cm. Since 25 > 17, both tangent types exist.
items.beginner_bridge: Draw the right triangle for one tangent type, identify the offset, and only then compare the two constructions.
items.shortcut_limit: L^2-M^2 = 4rR assumes both tangent segments are defined. A nonzero transverse segment requires centre distance greater than r+R; equality is the degenerate zero-length boundary.
items.mastery_check: Explain why the centre distance cancels from the difference but still controls whether both tangents exist.

items.question: Statements: Some archivists are cyclists. No cyclist is a reader. Conclusions: I. Some archivists are not readers. II. No archivist is a reader. III. Some cyclists are archivists. Which conclusions must follow?
steps: Choose a witness who is both an archivist and a cyclist; the first statement guarantees at least one.
That witness cannot be a reader, proving I.
The same witness proves III by reversing the membership description of a some-statement.
II need not hold: another archivist could be a reader while not being a cyclist. Both statements would still be true.

wrong_options.1: Misses the valid conversion of a some-statement.
wrong_options.2: Treats one known non-reader archivist as evidence about every archivist.
wrong_options.4: Overgeneralizes the existential witness to all archivists.

items.beginner_bridge: Use named example members to distinguish some from all before drawing Venn regions.
items.shortcut_limit: Some A are B converts to some B are A. All A are B does not convert to all B are A.
items.mastery_check: Construct a valid model where II is false; copying a single convenient diagram is insufficient.

items.question: An encoder reverses a four-letter word, then moves letters in positions 1 and 3 forward by one place and letters in positions 2 and 4 forward by two places. Alphabet movement wraps from Z to A. What is the code for RISK?
steps: Reverse RISK to KSIR.
Position 1: K becomes L. Position 2: S becomes U.
Position 3: I becomes J. Position 4: R becomes T.
Keep the transformed positions in order: LUJT.

wrong_options.1: Applies the shifts to the original word without reversing it.
wrong_options.3: Moves every reversed letter forward by one.
wrong_options.4: Reverses the completed output a second time.

items.beginner_bridge: Practise reversal and uniform shifts separately before combining a reversal with alternating shifts.
items.shortcut_limit: Position numbers refer to the reversed word. In an inferred-rule question, verify every supplied example rather than a single pair of letters.
items.mastery_check: Apply the stated rule to a new word containing Y or Z, and explain the wraparound.

items.question: A training centre recorded completed modules as follows: Group A: 36 in year 1 and 45 in year 2; Group B: 54 and 63; Group C: 30 and 42. By what percentage does the year-2 average for groups A and C exceed the year-1 average for all three groups?
steps: Year-2 total for A and C is 45+42 = 87; the average over two groups is 43.5.
Year-1 total for all groups is 36+54+30 = 120; the average over three groups is 40.
The increase is 43.5-40 = 3.5, compared with the year-1 base 40.
Percentage increase = 3.5/40 x 100 = 8.75%. The two divisors cannot cancel because the group counts differ.

wrong_options.2: Compares both years' totals for all three groups.
wrong_options.3: Compares the year-2 A/C total with the year-1 B/C total.
wrong_options.4: Compares totals 87 and 120 directly, ignoring different group counts.

items.beginner_bridge: Select table cells first, calculate each average separately, then identify the reference average for the percentage.
items.shortcut_limit: Ratios of averages reduce to ratios of totals only when the compared groups have equal counts.
items.mastery_check: Explain which mistake changes 8.75% higher into 27.5% lower.
